And Jacob lifted his eyes and saw, and look, Esau was coming, and four hundred men with him. And he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two female slaves.
And he put the female slaves and their children first, and Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph after them.
And he himself passed on ahead of them, and he bowed down to the ground seven times, until he came close to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him and embraced him, and he fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
And he lifted his eyes and saw the women and the children, and he said, "Who are these to you?" And he said, "The children with whom God has favored your servant."
And the female slaves came close, they and their children, and they bowed down.
And Leah also came close, and her children, and they bowed down, and afterward Joseph came close, and Rachel, and they bowed down.
And he said, "What is all this camp of yours that I met?" And he said, "To find favor in the eyes of my lord."
And Esau said, "I have plenty. My brother, let what is yours be yours."
And Jacob said, "Please, no! If I have found favor in your eyes, please take my present from my hand, since I have seen your face as one sees the face of God, and you have accepted me.
Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has favored me, and because I have everything." And he pressed him, and he took it.
And he said, "Let us travel on and go, and let me go in front of you."
And he said to him, "My lord knows that the children are tender, and the flocks and the cattle that are nursing are in my care, and if they are driven hard for one day, all the flocks will die.

Please let my lord pass on ahead of his servant, and as for me, I will move along slowly, at the pace of the livestock that are ahead of me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir."

And Esau said, "Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me." And he said, "Why is that? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord [alt: Why is it that I should find favor in the eyes of my lord?]."
And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
And Jacob traveled to Succoth, and he built himself a house, and for his herds he made shelters. That is why the place was named Succoth. [In Hebrew the name "Succoth" means "shelters."]
And Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem [alt: came to Salem, a city of Shechem], which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-Aram, and he camped in front of the city.
And he bought the plot of the field where he had pitched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitahs.
And he set up an altar there, and he called it "God, the God of Israel."
